mainTopic: Crossing water in shoes on שבת, cooling off and damp cloths on יום הכפורים, and permitting בכורות
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a future spring that flows from the בית המקדש and grows into a river where people become טהור. רב יוסף draws a hint from it about how deep a נדה must immerse, but the הלכה does not follow him. The גמרא then asks about crossing water on שבת: a מנעל may be worn, while for a סנדל רב אשי says not to cross לכתחילה. A story about רבינא missing the ריש גלותא's lecture shows that ruling followed in practice. Next come rules for יום הכפורים: sitting on wet clay is forbidden, cooling off with fruit or similar things is allowed, and the אמוראים argue about cooling off with a cup. Two reports of רבי יהושע בן לוי's damp-cloth practice on יום הכפורים and תשעה באב are compared, and the concern of סחיטה supports רבה בר מרי's version. Then רבי אלעזר is asked whether a senior scholar needs the נשיא's permission to permit בכורות. רבי אבא retells the story brought as proof, and the real question turns out to be about a suspected כהן; the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The amud ends with a new question about going out in a certain kind of sandal, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The future spring grows into a purifying river
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes a future spring that bubbles from under the threshold of the בית המקדש. It grows until it becomes a river where זבין, זבות, נדות, and יולדות can immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the future, water will come bubbling out from under the threshold of the בית המקדש. From there it will keep growing stronger and rising until it reaches the opening of בית דוד. Once it reaches the opening of בית דוד, it becomes a flowing river in which זבין, זבות, נדות, and יולדות bathe to become pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that describes a miraculous spring of the future, which starts small at the בית המקדש and grows into a full river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water starts as a small bubbling flow and keeps getting stronger as it travels. By the time it reaches בית דוד, it is a real flowing river. A river like this is valid for טבילה, so people with different kinds of טומאה can use it to become טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: bubbling up, flowing out in a small trickle
the threshold of the House, meaning the בית המקדש
David's house; some explain it as his burial place outside Jerusalem
a flowing, rushing river
men and women made טמא by a bodily discharge
women after childbirth

phrases.english: In the future, they will come out bubbling
from under the threshold of the Temple.
From here onward, it grows stronger and rises
until it reaches the opening of David's house.
Once it reaches the opening of David's house,
it becomes like a flowing river
in which zavim and zavot bathe,
as well as menstruating women and women after childbirth,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְפַכִּין עֲתִידִין לִהְיוֹת יוֹצְאִין מִתַּחַת מִפְתַּן הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, a spring from the בית המקדש will grow into a river that can purify people who are טמא.

steps.title: The verse from זכריה supports the description
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק in זכריה about a fountain opened for בית דוד and the people of ירושלים for purification.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'On that day there shall be a fountain opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for purification and for sprinkling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק as the source for its description of the purifying river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions three details: a fountain, בית דוד, and purification, including ולנדה. These match the ברייתא's picture: the water passes בית דוד and is used to purify people, including a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said; introduces a פסוק as a source
an opened fountain or spring
for purification and for removing טומאה

phrases.english: as it is said:
"On that day there shall be a fountain opened
for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem
for purification and for sprinkling."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for the description in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The description of a future purifying river passing בית דוד

steps.title: רב יוסף finds a hint about how deep a נדה must immerse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says this source hints that a נדה must be able to sit in water up to her neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: From here there is a hint that a נדה needs to be able to sit in the water up to her neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף takes the description of the purifying waters and draws a practical hint from it about how much water a נדה needs for טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source links these waters to purifying a נדה. רב יוסף uses that link to suggest a depth requirement: the water should reach her neck while she sits. He calls it only a רמז, a hint, not a full דרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: a hint or allusion, weaker than a full derivation
a woman who is טמאה because of her menstrual period
her neck

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From here there is an allusion regarding a menstruating woman,
that she must sit in water up to her neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִכָּאן רֶמֶז לְנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a הלכה-related hint from the ברייתא and the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף, the water for a נדה's טבילה should reach her neck.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow רב יוסף's hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that רב יוסף's hint is not the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no rule that the water must reach a woman's neck. One explanation is that as long as the מקוה has enough water to cover the whole body, it is kosher, so the specific depth does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: and the הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: A מקוה only needs enough water to cover the whole body; there is no neck-depth requirement.

phrases.english: But the halakha is not in accordance with his opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִילְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practical conclusion of step 3 and closes the side topic.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's view only as practical הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The depth of the water does not matter, as long as it covers the entire body.

steps.title: Crossing water on שבת while wearing shoes
steps.stepSummary: Returning to crossing water for a מצוה, the גמרא notes that on יום הכפורים there is no problem because people go barefoot. It then asks what the rule is on שבת, when people wear shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out on יום הכפורים, when there are no shoes. But on שבת, when people wear shoes, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side topic and goes back to its main discussion: crossing water to do a מצוה. It now asks how this works on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, wearing a מנעל is forbidden, so a person crosses barefoot and there is no concern. On שבת, people wear shoes. The worry is that a shoe might come off in the water and the person might pick it up and carry it, which is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: it works out well; used to grant one case before asking about another
a shoe, closed and fitting tightly
what is the rule?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about getting wet on שבת. The concern is that the shoe might fall off and the person would end up carrying it.

phrases.english: (It works out well on Yom Kippur,
when there are no shoes.)
But on Shabbat, when there are shoes, what is the rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דְּלֵיכָּא מִנְעָל, שַׁבָּת דְּאִיכָּא מִנְעָל, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier sugya (from the previous amud) about crossing water for a מצוה, after the side discussion in steps 1-4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one cross water on שבת while wearing shoes, given the risk of the shoe falling off and being carried?

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי crossed while wearing shoes
steps.stepSummary: נחמיה, the son-in-law of the נשיא's family, testifies that he saw רבי אמי and רבי אסי cross a pool of water while wearing their shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחמיה, the son-in-law of the house of the נשיא, said: I saw רבי אמי and רבי אסי come to a pool of water, and they crossed it while wearing their shoes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a story: great אמוראים crossed water on שבת without taking off their shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof from actual practice, a מעשה. Since these Sages crossed while wearing shoes, it is permitted. A shoe fits snugly and can be tied tightly, so we do not worry that it will fall off.

keyTerms.meaning: the son-in-law of the family of the נשיא
a pool or stream of water
in the manner of wearing, with the shoes still on the feet

phrases.english: Neḥemya,
the son-in-law of the house of the Nasi, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: I saw Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
when they came to a pool of water,
and they crossed it while wearing their shoes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר נְחֶמְיָה חַתְנֵיהּ דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה: אֲנָא חֲזֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted to cross water on שבת while wearing a מנעל.

steps.title: What about a סנדל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that a מנעל is fine, but asks about a סנדל, which sits loosely on the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out for a shoe. But what is there to say about a sandal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the question one step further, from a tight shoe to a loose sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנעל is tied tightly, so it will not slip off. A סנדל is looser, so it may come off in the water, and the person might carry it. The proof from רבי אמי and רבי אסי therefore may not cover sandals.

keyTerms.meaning: a sandal, which sits loosely on the foot
what is there to say?

phrases.english: It works out well for a shoe,
but what is there to say about a sandal?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח מִנְעָל, סַנְדָּל מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 6 to a מנעל and raises a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one cross water on שבת while wearing a loose סנדל?

steps.title: רבינא crossed while wearing a סנדל
steps.stepSummary: רב ריחומי testifies that he saw רבינא cross water while wearing sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ריחומי said: I saw רבינא cross while wearing sandals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the sandal question with another eyewitness story, this time permitting even a סנדל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier proof, this answer comes from what a great Sage actually did. רבינא did not take off his sandals, which suggests that even a loose סנדל is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: I saw him

phrases.english: Rav Riḥumi said:
I saw Ravina
crossing while wearing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב רִיחוּמִי: אֲנָא חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Based on רבינא's practice, one may cross even while wearing a סנדל.

steps.title: רב אשי says not to cross in a סנדל from the outset
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that one should not cross water in a סנדל לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: With a sandal, one should not cross from the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי disagrees with the lenient story and rules that a person should not plan to cross water wearing a סנדל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a סנדל is loose, it might fall off, and the person might pick it up and carry it on שבת. רב אשי therefore says not to do it לכתחילה. His wording suggests that if someone already did it, it is not treated as a serious violation.

keyTerms.meaning: from the outset, as the proper way to act in the first place

steps.whatToRemember: A מנעל may be worn while crossing water on שבת. With a סנדל, רב אשי says not to cross לכתחילה, because of the worry that it will fall off and be carried.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a הלכה can depend on a small physical detail: how securely the footwear is attached to the foot.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
With a sandal, not ab initio.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סַנְדָּל לְכַתְּחִלָּה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the lenient implication of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not cross water on שבת wearing a סנדל לכתחילה.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא visits and רבינא is absent
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא came to give a lecture in רב נתן's study hall in הגרוניא. רפרם and all the rabbis came, but רבינא did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא came to הגרוניא, to רב נתן's study hall. רפרם and all the רבנן came to the lecture. רבינא did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a short story connected to רב אשי's ruling about sandals from Step 9. This line sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not showing up to the ריש גלותא's lecture could look like disrespect. The rest of the story explains why רבינא stayed away, and that reason ends up tied to the הלכה we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the official leader of the Jews in Babylonia
Happened to come / visited
A public lecture, often given on שבת or a festival

phrases.english: The Exilarch came to Hagronya
to the house (study hall) of Rav Natan.
Rafram and all the Rabbis came to the lecture,
Ravina did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא אִיקְּלַע לְהַגְרוֹנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will show רב אשי's ruling (Step 9) being followed in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבינא was absent from the ריש גלותא's lecture.

steps.title: רפרם asks רבינא why he did not come
steps.stepSummary: The next day, רפרם wants to clear רבינא in the eyes of the ריש גלותא, so he asks him in public why he missed the lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day, רפרם wanted to remove any bad feeling toward רבינא from the mind of the ריש גלותא. He said to him: Why did the Master not come to the lecture?
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם asks רבינא a question. His goal is to give רבינא a chance to explain himself in front of the ריש גלותא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is friendly, not an attack. רפרם wants רבינא's good reason to come out in public so the ריש גלותא will not be insulted.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove from someone's mind, meaning to clear up a bad impression
"The Master", a respectful way to say "you"

phrases.english: The next day, Rafram wanted to remove Ravina
from the (negative) mind of the Exilarch,
He said to him: What is the reason
the Master did not come to the lecture?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתָא מָר לְפִירְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the dialogue about why רבינא was absent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבינא did not attend the lecture.

steps.title: רבינא says his foot hurt
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that his foot was hurting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My foot was hurting me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives his first reason: his foot hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer opens a series of suggestions from רפרם. Each suggestion is a way רבינא could still have come, and each one gets answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Hurting / in pain
My foot / my leg

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲוָה כָּאֵיב לִי כַּרְעַאי.
phrases.english: He said to him: My foot was hurting me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲוָה כָּאֵיב לִי כַּרְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רפרם's question.

steps.title: רפרם suggests he should have worn shoes
steps.stepSummary: רפרם pushes back: if your foot hurt, you could have worn shoes and come.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should have put on shoes.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם challenges the excuse. A sore foot does not stop you from walking if you wear shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says the excuse is not enough, because there was an easy fix. רבינא now has to explain why shoes would not have helped.

keyTerms.meaning: You should have
To put on shoes

phrases.english: You should have put on shoes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לָךְ לְמֵיסַם מְסָאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the excuse from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a sore foot kept רבינא home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shoes would have protected the foot, so he could have come.

steps.title: The pain was in the back of the foot
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the pain was in the back of his foot, where a shoe presses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was the back of the foot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers that shoes would not help, because the sore spot was at the heel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A closed shoe rubs against the back of the foot. So wearing one would make the pain worse, not better.

keyTerms.meaning: The back of the foot (the heel area)

phrases.english: It was the back of the foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבָּא דְכַרְעָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the shoe suggestion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shoes press on the heel, which was exactly where it hurt.

steps.title: רפרם suggests sandals
steps.stepSummary: רפרם suggests that רבינא could have worn sandals, which leave the heel open.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should have put on sandals.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם offers a second fix. Sandals do not cover the heel, so they would not hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers רבינא's heel problem directly. It also brings sandals into the story, which links back to רב אשי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: To put on (literally, to throw on)

phrases.english: You should have put on sandals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לָךְ לְמִרְמֵא סַנְדָּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from Step 14 with a new option.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סנדל leaves the heel open, so it would not cause pain.

steps.title: There was water on the way
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that there was a pool of water on the road that he would have had to cross.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There was a pool of water on the way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains that sandals were not a good option, because the road had water he would need to walk through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings the story right into the question from Steps 7-9: crossing water while wearing sandals on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A pool or stretch of water
The road / the way

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עוּרְקְמָא דְמַיָּא הֲוָה בְּאוֹרְחָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: There was a pool of water on the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עוּרְקְמָא דְמַיָּא הֲוָה בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sandal suggestion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sandals would have let him come.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water on the road made sandals a problem.

steps.title: רפרם says he could have crossed wearing the sandals
steps.stepSummary: רפרם says: just cross the water while wearing the sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should have crossed it in the manner of wearing (with the sandals on your feet).
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם gives a third fix: walk through the water with the sandals on, so you are not carrying them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing something is not carrying, so walking through the water with sandals on seems fine. This sets up רבינא's final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: In the manner of wearing (as clothing, not carrying)
To cross it

phrases.english: You should have crossed it in the manner of wearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לָךְ לְמֶעְבְּרֵיהּ דֶּרֶךְ מַלְבּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the water excuse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the water prevented him from coming.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Crossing while wearing the sandals is not carrying, so it should be allowed.

steps.title: רבינא cites רב אשי's ruling on sandals
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers: Don't you hold like רב אשי, who said one should not cross water in a סנדל לכתחילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does the Master not hold of what רב אשי said: A sandal, from the outset, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives his final answer. He relies on רב אשי's ruling from Step 9, so he could not cross the water in sandals, and he had no way to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every option has now been ruled out: shoes hurt, and sandals could not be used to cross the water. This shows the ריש גלותא that רבינא's absence was about הלכה, not disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: Does the Master not hold this view?
From the outset / ideally

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows רב אשי's ruling was followed in practice: one should not cross water in a סנדל לכתחילה, even when that means missing the ריש גלותא's lecture.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms רב אשי's ruling as practical הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the Master not hold
of that which Rav Ashi said:
A sandal, from the outset, no?!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking: of course you agree, so I couldn't cross in sandals.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 and closes the story.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Crossing while wearing sandals is fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אשי forbids crossing in a סנדל לכתחילה, so רבינא could not come.

steps.title: Sitting on damp clay on יום הכפורים is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בר גרוגרות teaches that one may not sit on damp clay on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בר גרוגרות taught: It is forbidden to sit on clay on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about יום הכפורים. Sitting on wet clay is forbidden because it is like washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing is forbidden on יום הכפורים. The moisture from the clay that touches the body is treated like washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Clay / mud

phrases.english: Yehuda bar Gerogarot taught:
It is forbidden to sit on clay
on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי יְהוּדָה בַּר גְּרוֹגְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: indirect washing on יום הכפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sitting on damp clay on יום הכפורים is forbidden.

steps.title: Only when the clay is dripping wet
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי limits the rule to clay that is wet to the touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: And only with clay that is moist (wet to the touch).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי narrows the rule. Only wet clay is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dry or barely damp clay does not count as washing. The ban applies only when you can feel the wetness.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist / dripping wet

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
And (only) with moist clay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: וּבְטִינָא מְטַפַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only to wet clay.

steps.title: Wet enough to make something else wet
steps.stepSummary: אביי defines "wet": the clay must be wet enough to make something else wet.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And with something moist enough to make (something else) moist.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sharpens the definition of wet clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeling a little damp is not enough. The clay must be wet enough to pass its wetness on to something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet enough to make something else wet

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And with (clay) moist enough to moisten (other things).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וּבְטוֹפֵחַ עַל מְנָת לְהַטְפִּיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines more precisely the term from Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only clay wet enough to wet other things is forbidden.

steps.title: Cooling off with fruit is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that one may cool off with fruit on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is permitted to cool oneself with fruits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a ruling: touching cool fruit to the body is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit is cool but does not leave wetness on the body. So it is not like washing.

keyTerms.meaning: To cool oneself off
Fruits

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It is permitted to cool oneself with fruits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מוּתָּר לְהִצְטַנֵּן בְּפֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the wet clay: cooling without wetness is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooling with fruit on יום הכפורים is allowed.

steps.title: How the אמוראים cooled off in practice
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה cooled off with a squash, רבה with a baby, and רבא with a silver cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה cooled off with a squash. רבה cooled off with a baby. רבא cooled off with a silver cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists what the sages actually did. This supports the idea that cooling off without wetness is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these leave water on the body. A squash and a baby are cool to the touch, and the silver cup sets up the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: A squash / gourd
A baby
A silver cup

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would cool off with a squash.
Rabba would cool off with a baby,
Rava would cool off with a silver cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה מִצְטַנֵּן בְּקָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of Step 22 in practice.
steps.raayaObject: Cooling off without wetness is allowed on יום הכפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב יהודה, רבה, and רבא.

steps.title: רב פפא: full versus not-full cups
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a full silver cup is forbidden and one that is not full is allowed. A clay cup is forbidden either way, because water seeps through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A silver cup, if full, is forbidden; if not full, it is permitted. A clay cup is forbidden both ways, because it seeps.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains when רבא's silver cup method is allowed. He also says a clay cup is never allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full cup might spill water onto the person. A clay cup lets water soak through its walls, so the body gets wet either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Full
Not full
Earthenware / clay
It seeps through

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: A silver cup,
full: forbidden; not full: permitted.
A clay one: both this and that are forbidden,
because it seeps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כָּסָא דְכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits on רבא's practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full silver cup is forbidden and a not-full one is allowed. A clay cup is always forbidden.

steps.title: רב: even a not-full silver cup is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב (some read רב אשי) rules that even a silver cup that is not full is forbidden, because it might slip and spill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A silver cup, even when not full, is also forbidden, because it might slip.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion disagrees with רב פפא about a cup that is not full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא worried only about a full cup spilling. This view worries that any cup with water might slip from the hand and wet the person.

keyTerms.meaning: It slips / spills
Also

steps.whatToRemember: Cooling off is allowed on יום הכפורים only if there is no real chance of getting wet. Clay that wets, a clay cup, and a full cup are forbidden. A not-full silver cup is disputed.
steps.confusionAlert: The text says "רב", but some read it as רב אשי. Either way, this view argues with רב פפא.

phrases.english: Rav said: A silver cup,
not full: also forbidden,
because it may slip (and spill).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: כָּסָא דְכַסְפָּא, חָסֵר — נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא about the not-full cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a not-full silver cup is forbidden because it may slip.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי's wet-cloth practice
steps.stepSummary: זעירא בר חמא tells רב יוסף what his father, רבי יהושע בן לוי, did: he prepared a damp cloth before יום הכפורים and before תשעה באב and used it the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירא בר חמא hosted רבי אמי, רבי אסי, רבי יהושע בן לוי, and all the Sages of קיסרי. He said to רב יוסף, the son of רבי יהושע בן לוי: 'Son of a lion! Come, let me tell you a wonderful thing your father used to do. On ערב יום הכפורים he would soak a cloth in water and squeeze it until it was almost dry. The next day he wiped his face, hands, and feet with it. On ערב תשעה באב he would soak the cloth in water, and the next day he passed it over his eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about how a great אמורא got some moisture on his body on fast days without actually bathing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the earlier steps about cooling off on יום הכפורים. The cloth is prepared the day before, so nothing is soaked on the fast day itself. As the next steps show, there is a question about which practice belonged to which fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: Host, someone who gives guests a place to stay
Son of a lion, a title of honor
Cloth or towel
Dry cloths, meaning squeezed until almost dry
Wipes

phrases.english: Ze'eira bar Chama, the host
of Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
and of all the Sages of Caesarea, he was.
He said to Rav Yosef,
the son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
Son of a lion!
Come, let me tell you a wonderful thing
that your father used to do:

phrases.aramaic: מִטְפַּחַת הָיָה לוֹ בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: He had a cloth on the day before Yom Kippur,
and he would soak it in water,
and make it like dry cloths,
phrases.notes: He wrung it out until it was almost dry.

phrases.english: and the next day he would wipe with it
his face, his hands, and his feet.

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב, שׁוֹרֶה אוֹתָהּ בְּמַיִם,
phrases.english: On the day before the Ninth of Av, he would soak it in water,
and the next day pass it over his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא אֵימָא לָךְ מִילְּתָא מְעַלַּיְתָא דַּהֲוָה עָבֵיד אֲבוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of cooling off on יום הכפורים with a practice of a great אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: Ways to get moisture on the body on fast days without bathing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי יהושע בן לוי, reported by זעירא בר חמא

steps.title: רבה בר מרי's version with the fast days switched
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי reports the same practice with the two fast days switched. On תשעה באב the wet cloth is used for the face, hands, and feet. On יום הכפורים the almost-dry cloth is only passed over the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה בר מרי came, he said: On ערב תשעה באב they bring a person a cloth. He soaks it in water and puts it under his head, and the next day he wipes his face, hands, and feet with it. On ערב יום הכפורים they bring him a cloth. He soaks it in water and squeezes it almost dry, and the next day he only passes it over his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of the same practice, but the two fast days are reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version יום הכפורים gets the stricter treatment. The cloth is nearly dry and only touches the eyes. On תשעה באב, where washing is forbidden only מדרבנן, he may use a wetter cloth for the face, hands, and feet. This makes sense because יום הכפורים is the more serious day.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly, when [he] came (from ארץ ישראל)
Under his head, at his pillow
He passes it over his eyes

steps.confusionAlert: The two reports look almost the same, but which fast day goes with which practice is switched. Read them side by side. In רבה בר מרי's version, יום הכפורים gets only the eyes.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, אָמַר:
phrases.english: And similarly, when Rabba bar Mari came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב מְבִיאִין לוֹ מִטְפַּחַת
phrases.english: On the day before the Ninth of Av, they bring him a cloth,
and he soaks it in water
and places it under his head,
and the next day he wipes his face, hands, and feet.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְבִיאִין לוֹ מִטְפַּחַת
phrases.english: On the day before Yom Kippur, they bring him a cloth,
and he soaks it in water,
and makes it like dry cloths,
and the next day he passes it over his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing report of the practice in step 26, with the two fast days reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום הכפורים, only an almost-dry cloth over the eyes. On תשעה באב, a wet cloth may be used for the face, hands, and feet.

steps.title: The reversed version was rejected because of wringing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב tells רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא that he once taught the practice the opposite way, and they challenged him from the איסור of סחיטה. This confirms רבה בר מרי's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: You told us the opposite version, and we challenged you from the איסור of wringing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב explains why the reversed version cannot be right. A wet cloth on יום הכפורים could lead to wringing out water, which is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wet cloth were used on יום הכפורים for the face, hands, and feet, water might be squeezed out of it. סחיטה is forbidden on יום הכפורים just as on שבת. So the wetter cloth must belong to תשעה באב, as רבה בר מרי reported.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, reversed
We challenged you
Wringing or squeezing liquid out, a מלאכה forbidden on שבת and יום הכפורים

steps.whatToRemember: On יום הכפורים, only an almost-dry cloth over the eyes is allowed, because a wet cloth raises a concern of סחיטה. The wetter cloth is for תשעה באב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said
to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
You told us the opposite,
and we challenged you from wringing.
phrases.notes: Wringing is forbidden on יום הכפורים, so a wet cloth cannot be used then.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיפְּכָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן, וְאוֹתֵיבְנָךְ סְחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה בר מרי's version (step 27). רבי יעקב recalls that רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא's reversed version, which had a wetter cloth on יום הכפורים, was challenged from סחיטה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The version that allows a wet cloth for the face, hands, and feet on יום הכפורים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Using a wet cloth on יום הכפורים risks סחיטה, which is forbidden on that day.

steps.title: Does a זקן sitting in the ישיבה need the נשיא's permission to permit בכורות?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רבי אלעזר is asked whether a זקן who sits in the ישיבה must get permission to permit בכורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר תחליפא said in the name of רב עמרם, who said in the name of רבה בר בר חנה: They asked רבי אלעזר: Does a זקן who sits in the ישיבה need to get permission (from the נשיא) to permit בכורות, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question asked of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may not be eaten unless it has a permanent מום. Judging this takes expert knowledge, so permission from the נשיא was normally required. The question is whether a senior scholar is exempt from asking.

keyTerms.meaning: A senior scholar who sits in the academy
To get permission
To permit firstborn animals (by judging their blemishes)

phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa said
that Rav Amram said
that Rabba bar bar Chana said:
They asked Rabbi Elazar:
An elder who sits in the academy,
must he get permission to permit firstborn animals,
or does he not need to?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, unrelated to the cloth practices.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a זקן who sits in the ישיבה must get the נשיא's permission to permit בכורות

steps.title: What exactly were they unsure about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the basis of the question was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What were they asking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask why this was a question at all. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since permission is normally required, the גמרא wants to know what side might make a senior scholar different. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it that they were asking? (a request to explain the doubt)

phrases.english: What were they asking?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the question in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind each side of the doubt

steps.title: The two sides: honoring the נשיא versus the זקן's stature
steps.stepSummary: Based on רב אידי בר אבין, this power was given to the נשיא's household to raise its stature, so perhaps everyone must ask. Or perhaps a זקן sitting in the ישיבה is important enough that he need not ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were asking. רב אידי בר אבין said: This power was left to the house of the נשיא so that they would be honored through it. So perhaps a person must still get permission. Or perhaps, since he is a זקן who sits in the ישיבה, he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides of the question asked to רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission rule exists to give honor to the נשיא, not only to check that the expert is qualified. If honor is the reason, even a great scholar should ask. On the other hand, a senior scholar's own standing might exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish community
To raise their stature through it
Or perhaps

phrases.english: This is what they were asking:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Like what Rav Idi bar Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה הִנִּיחוּ לָהֶם לְבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
phrases.english: This matter was left to the house of the Nasi
so that they would gain stature through it.
So he must get permission;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּזָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב בִּישִׁיבָה,
phrases.english: or perhaps, since he is an elder who sits in the academy,
he does not need to.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָא מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30 by laying out both sides of the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permission exists to honor the נשיא, so it may apply to everyone. Or a senior scholar's standing may exempt him.

steps.title: Eyewitness proof that even a great elder asked permission
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק בן חקולא testifies that he saw רבי יוסי בן זימרא, a זקן sitting in the ישיבה and greater than the current נשיא's grandfather, ask permission to permit בכורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי צדוק בן חקולא stood up and said: I saw רבי יוסי בן זימרא, who was a זקן who sat in the ישיבה and was of higher standing than this נשיא's grandfather, and he still asked permission to permit בכורות.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone in the ישיבה stands up and answers the question with an eyewitness report. Even a great זקן asked for permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone this great still asked the נשיא, then being a זקן in the ישיבה does not exempt a person. This supports the side that permission is needed, because the purpose is to honor the נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: He stood up on his feet (to testify)
I saw, an eyewitness report
Of higher standing than this one's grandfather (the current נשיא's grandfather)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי צדוק בן חקולא's report seems to prove that even a זקן who sits in the ישיבה must ask the נשיא's permission. But רבי אבא disputes the story in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי צָדוֹק בֶּן חָקוֹלָא עַל רַגְלָיו, וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tzadok ben Chakola stood on his feet and said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא,
phrases.english: I saw Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra,
who was an elder who sat in the academy,
and who stood at a higher rank than this one's grandfather,
phrases.notes: Some read this as 'who stood before the grandfather of this נשיא.' Either way, he was a figure of great standing.

phrases.english: and he still took permission to permit firstborn animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבִּי צָדוֹק בֶּן חָקוֹלָא עַל רַגְלָיו, וְאָמַר: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an eyewitness proof for the question of steps 29 to 31. Step 33 rejects this proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a זקן who sits in the ישיבה must still get permission
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי צדוק בן חקולא saw רבי יוסי בן זימרא ask permission to permit בכורות
steps.whyThisMatters: If the story were accurate, it would show that the permission requirement is about honoring the נשיא and applies even to the greatest scholars. Step 33 challenges exactly this.

steps.title: רבי אבא says the story happened differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rejects רבי צדוק בן חקולא's version of the incident. He points out that רבי יוסי בן זימרא was a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: That is not how the incident happened. Rather, this is how it happened: רבי יוסי בן זימרא was a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא says the story just quoted as a proof did not happen that way. He begins retelling it by noting that רבי יוסי בן זימרא was a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 32 depended on reading the story as a request for permission from the נשיא. רבי אבא takes that proof apart by adding one key fact: the man was a כהן. A כהן has a personal stake in בכורות, so his question must have been about something else entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not how the incident happened
Rather
A priest; the בכור goes to him

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא is not arguing about the הלכה of asking the נשיא. He is saying the story cannot prove anything about that question, because it was about a different issue.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
The incident was not like this,
rather, this is how the incident was:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא כֹּהֵן הָיָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra was a priest,
phrases.notes: Today a כהן may eat a בכור only once it has a blemish. That gives him a personal interest in finding one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה, אֶלָּא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the factual basis of the proof brought in Step 32.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יוסי בן זימרא asking permission
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was told wrongly. Because he was a כהן, his question was about being suspected, not about getting the נשיא's permission.

steps.title: The real question: can a suspected person rule on the matter?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן זימרא's actual question was which view is the הלכה. רבי מאיר holds that a suspected person may not judge or testify on the matter. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that he is believed about someone else's case but not his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was asking: Is the הלכה like רבי מאיר, who said that someone suspected in a matter may not judge it or testify about it? Or is the הלכה like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said that he is believed about his friend's case but not about his own?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יוסי בן זימרא was really asking. He wanted to know which of two views about a suspected person is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a כהן gains when a בכור has a blemish, כהנים are considered חשוד in this area. According to רבי מאיר, a כהן could never examine בכורות at all. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he could examine another person's בכור but not his own.

keyTerms.meaning: He was asking / he had a doubt
One who is suspected in a matter
He may not judge it and may not testify about it
Or perhaps
Believed / trusted
His friend's (someone else's) case

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole story. It is no longer about honoring the נשיא's household. It is a general rule about whether a person with a personal interest can be trusted.

phrases.english: and this is what he was asking:
Is the halakha like Rabbi Meir, who said:
one who is suspect in a matter —
may not judge it and may not testify about it?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Or perhaps the halakha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: נֶאֱמָן הוּא עַל שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: who said: he is believed about his fellow's
but is not believed about his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבא's retelling by stating the actual question that was asked.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רבי מאיר (a suspected person may not judge at all) or רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (he is believed about others but not about himself).

steps.title: The answer: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The question was answered: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it for him: the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So a כהן may examine and permit another person's בכור, but not his own. This also closes off the proof from Step 32: the story was never about asking the נשיא for permission.

keyTerms.meaning: And he resolved it for him

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבא, the story was about a כהן who is suspected regarding בכורות, not about asking the נשיא's permission. The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a suspected person is believed about others, not about himself.

phrases.english: And he resolved it for him:
the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a suspected person is believed about his fellow's case but not about his own.

steps.title: A new question about going out in a certain sandal
steps.stepSummary: The same חכמים raise another question: may one go out wearing a sandal made of a certain material? The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also asked: What is the law about going out in a sandal made of…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about going out in a particular kind of sandal. It is setting up a question whose details continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְתוּ ("and further") shows that this is another question asked by the same group of חכמים. The topic moves away from בכורות to the material a sandal is made of.

keyTerms.meaning: And further / additionally
What is the law?
To go out
Sandal

What is the law regarding going out in a sandal made of
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ קָא מִבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question from the same series of questions that began in Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may go out wearing a sandal made of a certain material (completed on the next amud).
